newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden to propose selling 49 pct of Telia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sweden to propose selling 49 pct of Telia - paper.

text.p: Sweden's minority Social Democratic government will propose the sale of 49 percent of public telecoms company Telia, a Swedish daily business newspaper reported on Thursday.
The government would pocket 20 billion crowns ($2.6 billion) on the sale and Telia would then be able to get the five to ten billion crowns it needs for investments, Dagens Industri said.
The shares could be listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange at the beginning of 1998, the newspaper said.
"The government would need a parliamentary decision that authorises it to sell up to half of shares in Telia," the newspaper said.
"Parliament can take such a decision at the earliest this autumn, so a listing could come at the beginning of 1998."

Sweden's seven-party parliament has swung in favour of selling a part of Telia and the Left party is the only camp still opposed to a privatisation, according to an analysis of the Swedish telephone market by consulting group Procivitas.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 7.703 Swedish Crowns)
